# Contracts: Expanded Name Corpus

This feature exposes no network API. Its contracts are (1) the generated corpus
module's shape, (2) the build script's CLI, and (3) the UI behavior contract
that the rest of the app relies on.

## 1. Generated module — `src/lib/nameCorpus.ts`

Generated by `scripts/build-name-corpus.mjs`; committed; never hand-edited.

```ts
// Generated by scripts/build-name-corpus.mjs — do not edit by hand.
// Source: <source id> | Generated: <ISO date> | Counts: <girl>/<boy>
export const GIRL_CORPUS: string[]; // packed: "Emma,Olivia,…".split(",")
export const BOY_CORPUS: string[];
```

**Guarantees** (checked by `scripts/verify-name-corpus.mjs`):

- Ordered by descending popularity (births since `--since`) — index is rank.
- Each entry matches `/^[A-Z][A-Za-z'-]{1,14}$/`; no entry contains a comma,
  which would corrupt the packed representation.
- No duplicates within an array; no spelling in both arrays.
- Counts are within 10% of the expected ≈66,188 girl / ≈39,778 boy; a larger
  swing signals a source or parsing regression.
- Header comment records source and generation date for provenance.

**Consumers**: `src/BabyNameSwipe.tsx` only. Spec 002 may additionally read
rank (array index) for popularity-based criteria.

## 2. Build script — `scripts/build-name-corpus.mjs`

Plain Node (no dependencies), run manually by a developer.

```
node scripts/build-name-corpus.mjs [--source ssa|mirror] [--input <path>]
                                   [--limit <n-per-gender>] [--since <year>]
                                   [--out <path>]
```

| Flag | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--source` | `ssa` | `ssa` = authoritative `names.zip` from ssa.gov (verified reachable); `mirror` = public SSA-derived GitHub sources, offline fallback |
| `--input` | — | Local path to an already-downloaded archive, bypassing all network access |
| `--limit` | none | Optional cap on names per gender, applied after popularity ordering. Unset by default — the full corpus ships |
| `--since` | `1995` | Birth year floor for the popularity ranking (gender assignment always uses all-time counts) |
| `--out` | `src/lib/nameCorpus.ts` | Output path |

**Required request headers for `--source ssa`**: SSA is fronted by Akamai and
returns 403 to default HTTP agents. The script MUST send a full browser header
set — `User-Agent`, `Accept`, `Accept-Language`, `Sec-Fetch-Dest/Mode/Site/User`,
`Upgrade-Insecure-Requests`, `sec-ch-ua`, `sec-ch-ua-mobile`,
`sec-ch-ua-platform` — and should send a `Referer` of the babynames page for
the archive request. A 403 here is edge filtering, not a network-policy
denial; the script should say so in its error message.

**Do not commit the 7.5 MB source archive** — only the generated module.

**Behavior**: fetch → parse → curate (validity filter, gender assignment by
occurrence dominance, popularity ordering) → emit the module → print a summary
(per-gender counts, total, dropped counts by reason). Exits non-zero on any
invariant violation so a bad corpus is never written.

**Determinism**: same source + same flags produces a byte-identical module
apart from the generation timestamp in the header.

## 3. UI behavior contract (regression surface)

What must remain true after the swap — the observable contract the app already
has with its users:

| Behavior | Contract |
|---|---|
| Deck order | Both swipers encounter names in the same order; each is served only names they have not personally swiped; no name served twice |
| Card band color | Girl names pink, boy names blue, neutral slate whenever the filter is "both" — unchanged, driven by `g` |
| Gender filter | "girl"/"boy"/"both" select the corresponding pool exactly as today |
| Keeps list | Shows every name the current swiper kept, **including names absent from the corpus** |
| Matches list | Shows every name both swipers kept, **including names absent from the corpus** |
| Persistence | Same storage key, same shape; existing saves load unchanged with no migration step |
| Backup/restore | Round-trips all state exactly as today |
| Undo | Unchanged |

Any change to the left column is a breaking change to this feature.
